body: Income Tax Act 2007 section MB 1: Family scheme income is based on a person's net income and adjusted under subpart MB. Employment income, main benefit income, other income, and allowed deductions are treated as derived or incurred at uniform daily rates as stated. Certain exempt overseas pensions, maintenance payments, salary or wages exempt under listed Acts, PIE attributed income, and listed PIE distributions are included; certain maintenance payments are deductions.

Income Tax Act 2007 section MB 2: If a person's income is calculated for a period that is less or more than a year, family scheme income is adjusted by the formula person's family scheme income x 365 / days. Days is the total number of days in the period for which the income has been derived.

Income Tax Act 2007 section MB 3: For a family scheme activity, the income and deductions are ignored when calculating family scheme income if, treating the person as having only that activity's income and deductions, the person would have a net loss for the year. Two or more activities may be treated as 1 activity when normally carried on in association.

Income Tax Act 2007 section MB 4: Close-company family scheme income for a major shareholder is the greater of zero and the formula (person's interest + attributed interest) x (income - dividends), adjusted for main income equalisation account amounts. Attributed interest is dependent child interest / relevant major shareholders. A main income equalisation deposit is added to income; a main income equalisation refund is subtracted from income.

Income Tax Act 2007 section MB 5: A superannuation-scheme distribution is assessable income for family scheme income in the tax year or years corresponding to the income year or years in which employer contributions were made, excluding an amount attributable to the person's own contribution as a member of the scheme.

Income Tax Act 2007 section MB 6: A distribution of a retirement scheme contribution from a retirement savings scheme is assessable income of the person derived in the income year in which the distribution is made when the statutory conditions apply.

Income Tax Act 2007 section MB 7: Settlor trust family scheme income is calculated by the formula (trustee's adjusted net income + companies income) / settlor number. Trustee's adjusted net income is trustee net income reduced, not below zero, by beneficiary income vested or paid. Companies income is the greater of zero and the total of trustee's interest x (income - dividends) for relevant companies. Main income equalisation deposits are added to trustee adjusted net income or company income; refunds are subtracted.

Income Tax Act 2007 section MB 7B: For employees not covered by MB 8, family scheme income includes the amount by which employment income would be greater without a private-use motor vehicle benefit, and the value including fringe benefit tax of a short-term charge facility benefit if the total value excluding FBT is more than the lesser of 5% of salary or wages and $1,200.

Income Tax Act 2007 section MB 8: Family scheme income from fringe benefits for controlling shareholders applies when the person is an employee of a company in which the person and associated persons hold voting interests of 50% or more, and the company provides attributed fringe benefits. The included amount is the taxable value of attributed fringe benefits plus the company's FBT liability for the person.

Income Tax Act 2007 section MB 10: For certain exempt pensions and annuities, family scheme income includes half of the amount of pension or annuity derived in the income year and does not include the other half; the inclusion rate is 0.5.

Income Tax Act 2007 section MB 11: If a dependent child's relevant amounts for the income year are more than $500, family scheme income includes an amount calculated by the formula (child's amounts - $500) / principal caregivers. Principal caregivers is the number of people who are each a principal caregiver of the child.

Income Tax Act 2007 section MB 12: Family scheme income of a person for an income year includes the non-residents' foreign-sourced income for the income year of the person's spouse, civil union partner, or de facto partner.

Income Tax Act 2007 section MB 12B: When a person receives a trust payment in the income year, the payment is not beneficiary income, and the person is not the settlor, the amount of the payment is included in family scheme income. The Commissioner may determine circumstances in which a payment from a trust should be excluded, in which case the amount is not included.

Income Tax Act 2007 section MB 13: Family scheme income includes the value of payments paid or provided from any source and used to replace lost or diminished income of the person or family, or meet usual living expenses of the person or family, unless the payment is excluded under subsection (2). Exclusions include ordinary commercial loans, non-assessable property disposal proceeds, loan repayments, refunds, capital account business or investment payments that are not loans, deceased estate payments, gambling or New Zealand lottery winnings, local or public authority payments, debt forgiveness by a public authority, charitable distributions, and educational scholarships or bursaries.
